summary: Fast dispersive readout of a superconducting transmon qubit is demonstrated with 97(1) ns total measurement duration (from pulse start until measurement-induced π-pulse error drops below $10^{-4}$), achieving 0.17(1)% assignment error with a 58 ns pulse. Measurement-induced leakage is suppressed to $2.7(2) \times 10^{-5}$ per measurement by operating at small qubit–resonator detuning ($\omega_r/\omega_q = 1.24$) where multiphoton resonances are weak and traversed diabatically.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity, low-leakage qubit measurement is essential for quantum error correction, but achieving all three simultaneously in the small-detuning regime—where large dispersive shifts are readily available—has been uncertain due to the dense spectrum of multiphoton resonances.
method: A dedicated filter resonator with effective decay rate $\kappa_\mathrm{eff}/2\pi = 30.8$ MHz enables rapid photon depletion without active pulse circuits, combined with dispersive shift near the optimal SNR-per-photon condition ($|\chi|/2\pi \approx 9$ MHz, $J/2\pi = 24.4$ MHz). Assignment fidelity is characterized via heterodyne measurement using matched-filter weighting; measurement-induced state transitions are benchmarked with a leakage-sensitive three-level readout; and multiphoton resonance coupling is analyzed via Floquet simulations and Landau-Zener crossing rates.
result: Assignment error $\epsilon_\mathcal{F} = 0.17(1)\%$ with 58 ns pulse; measurement-induced leakage $P_\mathcal{L}^\mathrm{on} = 2.7(2) \times 10^{-5}$ (twice background); measurement-induced relaxation dominates with $T_1^\mathrm{meas} = 12.7$ µs; Floquet analysis shows dominant $|0\rangle$–$|10\rangle$ resonance has splitting $\Delta\varepsilon/2\pi \approx 54$ kHz and Landau-Zener leakage probability $P_L \sim 10^{-7}$ per traversal.
